segments.contextAfter: Raising a view’s layout priority encourages the higher priority view to shrink later when the group is shrunk and stretch sooner when the group is stretched.

segments.contextAfter:
```swift
HStack {
    Text("This is a moderately long string.")
        .font(.largeTitle)
        .border(Color.gray)

    Spacer()

    Text("This is a higher priority string.")
        .font(.largeTitle)
        .layoutPriority(1)
        .border(Color.gray)
}
```

segments.normalizedSource: ```swift HStack { Text("This is a moderately long string.") .font(.largeTitle) .border(Color.gray) Spacer() Text("This is a higher priority string.") .font(.largeTitle) .layoutPriority(1) .border(Color.gray) } ```
segments.contextBefore: Raising a view’s layout priority encourages the higher priority view to shrink later when the group is shrunk and stretch sooner when the group is stretched.
segments.contextAfter: In the example above, the first [`Text`](text.md) element has the default priority `0` which causes its view to shrink dramatically due to the higher priority of the second [`Text`](text.md) element, even though all of their other attributes (font, font size and character count) are the same.
